A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Curvature Tuning research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable matching and comparison. Internal numerical inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original toy-network experiments, ResNet and Swin transfer results, and adversarial and corruption robustness evaluations.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results and reports additional VGG-11 experiments, activation ablations, LoRA configuration comparisons, and finetuning robustness results.

M1.justification: The CTU mixture, shared steering parameter, and per-neuron trainable parameter pairs remain. Appendix D changes the forward computation by adding a denominator offset; Section 3.2 specifies numerical stabilization at beta = 1. Renaming CT and Trainable CT to S-CT and T-CT does not itself change the method.

E1.justification: The Imagenette pretraining scenario is removed: Swin experiments now use ImageNet-pretrained models. The twelve downstream classification datasets, CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet robustness benchmarks, and synthetic tasks remain. Adding VGG-11 changes model coverage rather than introducing another dataset or task.

E2.justification: v5 adds evaluated SiLU and Softplus comparators in Table S3 and includes LoRA in the new finetuning robustness comparison. Steering CT is removed from the Swin comparison. The main linear-probing and LoRA comparator families remain.

E3.justification: Swin evaluation changes from ReLU-modified models pretrained on Imagenette to ImageNet-pretrained GELU models, with new validation-based learning-rate searches. v5 also adds VGG-11, LoRA rank/scaling sweeps, and finetuning-before-robustness evaluation. Table S4 explicitly selects the best test accuracy across candidate scaling factors. Figure 2 changes hidden widths from 12/18 to 7.

E4.justification: New analyses test the CTU mixing choice against its SiLU and Softplus endpoints, sensitivity to LoRA rank/scaling, and T-CT robustness after ordinary finetuning. Figure 2 replaces the two-width capacity comparison with a single-width illustration. Existing ResNet parameter-distribution plots remain, while Swin distribution statistics and pretraining curves are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions use three runs with seeds 42, 43, and 44 and already show standard-deviation bands in selected figures. v5 substantially expands uncertainty reporting by providing standard deviations for benchmark accuracies, robustness results, and selected beta values in appendix tables. This does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v5 adds VGG-11, ablation, LoRA-sweep, and T-CT robustness results and replaces Swin results under changed conditions. The abstract's ResNet-50/152 gains over linear probing change from 7.14%/8.46% to 8.59%/8.34%, matching values already reported in v2's body. Retained table values also change, including Table 2's ResNet-50 l-infinity average from 10.68 to 9.76. Some v5 main/appendix results conflict.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C.2 substantially revise the circle-error derivation using explicit endpoints, region indices, and sign changes. The general biconditional becomes a one-way implication, with the converse restricted to regression. Appendix C.1 also revises the activation recurrence and introduces a restricted Sobolev-space characterization distinguishing weak and classical derivatives. The central projection theorem remains.

C1.justification: The central curvature-control, projection, and parameter-efficiency claims remain. v5 extends the robustness claim explicitly to T-CT and concludes that both variants exhibit an implicit bias toward robustness, whereas v2's robustness evidence and claims focused on steering CT.

C2.justification: The Swin discussion drops insufficient Imagenette pretraining as an explanation for underperformance and emphasizes limited coverage of attention mechanisms. Future directions shift toward attention-temperature modulation. Robustness improvements are newly interpreted as an implicit bias, and the earlier interpretation that larger models require less curvature adjustment is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 replaces the Swin pretraining recipe with explicit learning-rate search grids. Section 3.2 adds stabilization and GELU-approximation details. However, the stated stabilization constant of 1e-6 conflicts with 1e-63 in the trainable CTU listing. The code link and GPU disclosure remain.

R1.justification: v5 adds Srinivas et al.'s low-curvature-network work and distinguishes its pretraining approach from CT's activation-based PEFT positioning. RoAd is reclassified as additive PEFT. The ReLU Strikes Back and Mamba references and associated positioning are removed; the broader PEFT and spline literature remains.

P1.justification: v5 systematically introduces S-CT/T-CT terminology, swaps the finetuning and robustness subsections, and revises experimental discussion and conclusions. It adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. Much of the introduction, background, method exposition, and overall section hierarchy remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn from six panels to three, and the activation illustration's axes and color scale change. Benchmark tables are substantially restructured into appendix panels with uncertainty columns, alongside new ablation and robustness tables. Swin pretraining curves are removed; retained parameter-distribution plots are renumbered rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: Tables S3–S4 address v2's untested mixing choice and rank-one-only LoRA comparison. ImageNet/GELU Swin evaluation replaces the limited Imagenette/ReLU proxy, and systematic standard deviations make the evidence more assessable. These substantially strengthen validation of the paper's design and applicability. Conflicting robustness entries in Tables 2/S7, inconsistent Swin averages in Tables 4/S9, and the Appendix D stabilization typo weaken reproducibility, but remain localized relative to these gains.
